title: Strict finite open exchange over completed coefficient rings
statement:
Let $(A,I)$ satisfy [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], with $P_n=A/I^n$, and let $U'=U\times_X X'$ with open immersions $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, $j':U'\hookrightarrow X'$ and maps $g:X'\to X$, $g_U:U'\to U$ [def-cbc-open-immersion-square]. On every small pro-etale site use the completed ring $A_T=\varprojlim_n(P_n)_T$, the strict tower category $\operatorname{Tow}_A(T)$ and reduction $K_\bullet$ of the datum. Let $J_j,J_{j'}$ be termwise sheafified open extension [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf, def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Let $G_g,G_{g_U}$ be total derived levelwise module pullback on strict towers along the projection-induced completed ring maps, as in [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. Then, for every $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_U))$, there is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$b_K:G_g(J_jK_\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}J_{j'}G_{g_U}(K_\bullet)\quad\text{in }D(\operatorname{Tow}_A(X')).$$
Under the finite-coefficient comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence], its $n$-th component is the canonical finite exchange of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change] for $\Lambda=P_n$, with finite constant-coefficient pullback as in [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact],
$$g_n^*j_!K_n\xrightarrow{\sim}j'_!g_{U,n}^*K_n.$$
This isomorphism and its inverse arise from simultaneous strict diagram maps, commute with all quotient transitions, and are linear for the $A_{X'}$-actions through $A_{X'}\to(P_n)_{X'}$. The inverse finite component is the $j'_!\dashv j'^*$-adjoint mate of $g_U^*$ applied to the open unit, followed by the canonical inverse pullback-composition identification. No unrelated morphisms in evaluated derived categories are chosen to define $b_K$. No derived completeness, quasi-compactness or constructibility of $K$ is assumed, and no derived inverse limit is part of this assertion.

source.place: Finite-exchange/reduction identification before Rlim; Stacks 03DI, sites-modules.tex, lemma-extension-by-zero; completed-ring strict exchange is an agent-written refinement.

proof.text: Use the slice-site equivalences of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] for $j,j'$. The datum defines completed rings by compatible families of finite coefficient sections. Thus, on $V\to U$, $A_X|_U(V)=\varprojlim_n(P_n)_X(V)=\varprojlim_n(P_n)_U(V)=A_U(V)$, with the same operations, restrictions and projections. This also identifies $A_{X'}|_{U'}=A_{U'}$. The coefficient maps $c_g$ and $c_{g_U}$ of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] are compatible with these identifications: after each finite projection both are the constant-coefficient base-change map, and maps into the displayed limit agree when all projections agree. In particular the ring map on the localized square is exactly the map prescribed for $g_U$. No isomorphism $g^{-1}A_X=A_{X'}$ is asserted.

source.place: Restriction to localized sites; completed rings here are the sectionwise limits in the coefficient datum.

proof.text: Write $E=j_!$ and $E'=j'_!$ for sheafified module extension for the completed rings. By [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], these are exact and satisfy $E\dashv j^*$ and $E'\dashv j'^*$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] to $c_g,c_{g_U}$: ordinary module pullbacks $g^*,g_U^*$ have the corresponding module direct images as right adjoints, with actions through the adjunct ring maps. The composite-adjunction formula [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] therefore gives $L_1=g^*E\dashv R_1=j^*g_*$ and $L_2=E'g_U^*\dashv R_2=g_{U*}j'^*$. All these are adjunctions on sheaves over the completed rings, before deriving anything.

The site functor for $g$ is $V\mapsto X'\times_X V$, by [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Localize it at $U$ and apply [lem-weil-pbc-localize-ringed-site-morphism]. Its hypotheses hold because this is the continuous functor defining the pro-etale morphism, the sites use the fixed small skeleta, and step 1 identifies its restricted ring map. The cartesian square identifies $V\times_UU'$ with $V\times_XX'$ for every $V\to U$: a pair $(v,x')$ determines its unique $U'$-coordinate by the fibre-product property. Denote this isomorphism by $a_V:V\times_UU'\to V\times_XX'$. Its projections show it is natural in $V$. The localization theorem gives an $A_U$-linear natural isomorphism $t:R_1\xrightarrow{\sim}R_2$; on a sheaf $H$ its value at $V$ is $H(a_V):H(V\times_XX')\to H(V\times_UU')$. Its inverse is $H(a_V^{-1})$. Thus the comparison is specified also on scalar actions, rather than only on the underlying abelian sheaves.

Put $\delta=t^{-1}:R_2\to R_1$. Let $\eta_i,\varepsilon_i$ be the units and counits of the composite adjunctions of step 2. By [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] there is a natural isomorphism $\beta:L_1\to L_2$ characterized by $R_1(\beta_F)\eta_{1,F}=\delta_{L_2F}\eta_{2,F}$. Explicitly,
$$\beta_F=\varepsilon_{1,L_2F}\,L_1(\delta_{L_2F})\,L_1(\eta_{2,F}),\qquad
\gamma_F=\varepsilon_{2,L_1F}\,L_2(t_{L_1F})\,L_2(\eta_{1,F}).$$
The reverse conjugation gives $\gamma=\beta^{-1}$; uniqueness under the unit equation proves both composite identities. These formulas specify actual maps of completed-ring module sheaves. They use the sectionwise cartesian comparison from step 3 and so specify the canonical open exchange, not an arbitrary isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0B65 (lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints), applied to the two composite adjunctions.

proof.text:
For a strict tower complex $M_\bullet$, apply $\beta$ and $\gamma$ in each tower index and complex degree. If $d$ is its differential and $v_n:M_{n+1}\to M_n$ its transition, naturality gives
$$L_2(d)\beta=\beta L_1(d),\qquad L_2(v_n)\beta_{M_{n+1}}=\beta_{M_n}L_1(v_n),$$
and the same equations with $\gamma$ and $L_1,L_2$ interchanged. Hence these are inverse strict tower chain maps. The two composite identities hold in each degree and index already before localization. They are linear over $A_{X'}$ because each constituent in step 4 is a morphism in the module category. This is a simultaneous construction for every strict tower; it does not try to lift a family of morphisms in evaluated derived categories.

source.place: Degreewise application of the natural transformations constructed in step 4.

proof.text:
Represent $K_\bullet$ by a strict tower complex $M_\bullet$ and take one objectwise flat-term K-flat replacement $P_\bullet\to M_\bullet$ from [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-kflat-replacements], with the small index category $\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}}$. By [lem-cbc-ringed-open-flat-resolution], $EP_\bullet\to EM_\bullet$ is again such a replacement, including the original strict transitions. Exactness of $E'$ and levelwise exactness of towers give its termwise derived functor [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact, lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian, lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. Thus step 5 at $P_\bullet$ is a strict chain isomorphism
$$g^*EP_\bullet\xrightarrow{\beta_{P_\bullet}}E'g_U^*P_\bullet$$
representing $G_gJ_jK_\bullet\to J_{j'}G_{g_U}K_\bullet$, with inverse represented by $\gamma_{P_\bullet}$. The diagram replacement theorem says pullback preserves quasi-isomorphisms between these replacements. The resolving-class universal property [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class] then derives the two inverse natural transformations; their identities remain identities by that universal property. This makes the result natural in $K_\bullet$ and independent of the chosen replacement, hence also natural in $K$ through the reduction functor.

source.place: Strict diagram K-flat replacement and open K-flat preservation as stated by the cited nodes; resolving-class descent in derived.tex Tag 06XN.

proof.text: To identify the finite objects, use [lem-cbc-ringed-open-strict-reduction] for $j$: it gives the actual strict isomorphism $(j_!K)_\bullet\cong J_jK_\bullet$, represented on a K-flat $Q$ by $[p]\otimes b\mapsto[p\otimes b|_U]$. It applies to arbitrary $K$, with no quasi-compactness or completeness assumption. The finite-evaluation assertion in [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], applied to $j_!K$ and to $K$ for $g_U$, now identifies the evaluations of the two objects in step 6 with the restrictions of $g_n^*j_!K_n$ and $j'_!g_{U,n}^*K_n$. Here reduction of $j_!K$ as a $(P_n)_X$-complex is also part of the strict-reduction lemma. The comparisons are those of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence], and finite pullback is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact]. Thus $Lg_n^*$ and $Lg_{U,n}^*$ at these finite objects are represented by the specified exact finite module pullbacks, even when $K$ is unbounded. The normalized comparison existence is isolated in [lem-cbc-normalized-finite-comparison-existence]. Their uniqueness is proved by cancelling the finite model maps on K-flat representatives, where scalar-extension counits are invertible [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-tower], and using a K-flat resolution of an arbitrary complex to cancel the derived image of its quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Finite-exchange identification before derived inverse limits, with completed-ring typing supplied by the cited coefficient comparisons.

proof.text: Check the map under these identifications. The ringed open normalization [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] applies to $B_X=A_X,B_{X'}=A_{X'}$ and $c_g$, by step 1. It characterizes the inverse derived exchange as the $j'_!\dashv j'^*$-adjunct of $Lg_U^*u$ followed by the inverse pullback compositor, and says its restriction is the identity after the open unit identifications. The conjugation construction of steps 3-6 is this normalization: the right-adjoint comparison is exactly $H(a_V)$ and both composite units are the specified ones. The finite comparison preserves the open unit: on an extension summand it takes $p\mapsto[p]$ to $p\otimes a\mapsto[p\otimes a]$. Its balancing map is $(p\otimes b)\otimes a\mapsto p\otimes q(b)a$; inserting the unit gives $p\otimes1$ on either side. Restriction and base-change identifications use $a_V$ on both sides, and the structural ring maps agree after each projection by step 1. These equalities on tensor sections and extension summands descend by sheafification and by the K-flat comparisons of step 7. Therefore the inverse finite component has precisely the adjunct $g_{U,n}^*u$ followed by the inverse pullback-composition identification. By [lem-cbc-finite-open-exchange-scalars] this is the inverse of the canonical finite exchange of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change]. Uniqueness of an adjunction transpose identifies the inverse maps, and hence identifies $b_{K,n}$ with that finite exchange.

source.place: Tag 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero), explicit summand adjunction; ringed derived normalization and coefficient compatibility as stated in the cited nodes.

proof.text: For $b\ge a\ge1$, the finite-exchange scalar lemma applies to the finite-ring quotient $P_b\to P_a$. It says both normalized finite exchanges and their inverses commute with the strict semilinear quotient transitions, also as towers over a ring sheaf acting through compatible maps to the finite coefficient sheaves. The reduction tower has exactly these maps by [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], and the finite coefficient comparisons commute with them by [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]. Thus the identifications in steps 7-8 respect every quotient transition, not only adjacent ones. At level $n$, restriction of scalars through $A_{X'}\to(P_n)_{X'}$ gives the action in the statement, and the finite component maps and their inverses are linear for that action by [lem-cbc-finite-open-exchange-scalars]. Together with the strict representatives of step 6, this proves all the asserted compatibility clauses. The construction ended in $D(\operatorname{Tow}_A(X'))$; no inverse limit, completeness, quasi-compactness, or constructibility was used.
